leftEvidence.title: Kingdom seeking is placed before tomorrow

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus repeats the warning against anxious questions about necessities and contrasts the nations’ seeking with the Father’s knowledge.
points.right: Jesus commands asking, seeking, and knocking and states that each receives a corresponding result.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The hearers are told to seek God’s Kingdom and righteousness first and to leave tomorrow’s trouble to tomorrow.
points.right: Human parents’ good gifts become the lesser case for the heavenly Father giving good things.

payload.posture: Kingdom seeking and asking sayings both direct desire toward the Father’s knowledge and goodness.

rightEvidence.title: Asking is grounded in the Father’s goodness

payload.tension: The texts do not promise that anxious desire or every requested object is simply granted as imagined.
payload.title: Seeking first and continuing to ask
